header:
# Jericho municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 12; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 124 (Town of Jericho charter): section 3 and section 4: selectboard members are elected by Australian ballot; the board has five members

Town of Jericho, 2024-25 Town Report (official town website), 'Elected/Appointed Town Officials' pages: the pre-meeting board was Peter Booth (term to 2028), Catherine McMains (2026), Erik Johnson (2027), Amy Kapitan (interim, 2026), and Laura Crain (interim, 2026)

Town of Jericho, official election-night results, annual town meeting, March 3, 2026 (official town website): Amy Kapitan was elected to a three-year term (903 votes), Laura Crain to a two-year term (911), and Chris Brown to a one-year term (610, defeating Joseph Flynn, 485). The seated board is Booth, Johnson, Kapitan, Crain, and Brown; McMains is no longer a member. Kapitan and Crain sat as interim appointees before the 2026 meeting and were then elected. Jericho's Chris Brown is not Chris Brown of Rutland-3, the former state representative
Town of Jericho, official election-night results, annual town meeting, March 3, 2026 (official town website): David Barrington was re-elected Moderator for a one-year term (1,026 votes)
Town of Jericho, 2024-25 Town Report (official town website), 'Elected/Appointed Town Officials' pages: David Barrington is Town Moderator
Town of Jericho, official election-night results, annual town meeting, March 3, 2026 (official town website): Jessica R. Alexander was re-elected Town Clerk for a one-year term (1,115 votes)
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Jessica Alexander as Jericho's town clerk
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, town clerk contact spreadsheet (updated June 12, 2026): lists Jessica Alexander as Jericho's town clerk contact
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 124 (Town of Jericho charter): section 5: the selectboard appoints the Town Treasurer

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Brian Stevens as Jericho's town treasurer. The Secretary of State's treasurer spreadsheet carries no Jericho data and no town source publishes a different holder
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 124 (Town of Jericho charter): section 5: the selectboard appoints the collector of delinquent taxes
Town of Jericho, 2024-25 Town Report (official town website), 'Elected/Appointed Town Officials' pages: the appointed town officers table names Amy Morse as Delinquent Tax Collector

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 124 (Town of Jericho charter): section 5: the selectboard appoints three listers; neither the town's Lister and Assessor page nor the town report's appointed-officers table names them, so the post is created without memberships
Town of Jericho (official website), Cemetery Commission page: the commissioners are Robert Grandchamp (term expires 2026), Isabella Martin (2027), and Terry Hook (2029)

Town of Jericho, official election-night results, annual town meeting, March 3, 2026 (official town website): Terence B. Hook was elected to a three-year cemetery commissioner term (1,005 votes). The two-year seat drew no ballot candidate and only scattered write-ins (the leader had five); a write-in plurality alone does not seat a holder, and the town's commission page continues to seat Grandchamp, who is therefore carried as the third commissioner

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): names twelve justices of the peace for Jericho: Peter Booth, Tom Cheney, Kathleen Bassett Cramer, Tom Joslin, Cathy Paris, Carly Schuckers, Carol Kanter Smith, Megan Sullivan, Michael Sweeney, Michele Tulis, Mike Weinberg, and Jennifer Burton

Town of Jericho, 2024-25 Town Report (official town website), 'Elected/Appointed Town Officials' pages: the town report's justices of the peace block names the same twelve, 'elected November 2024 to a 2-year term beginning Feb. 1 2025'

Jennifer Burton of Jericho is a different person from Jennifer Burton of Johnson, also elected a justice of the peace in 2024; the office is town-bound
